rules.title: Namespace Naming
rules.check: Namespaces MUST use PascalCase and follow Company.Product.Feature pattern.
rules.bad_example:
namespace myApp.services.orders; // lowercase
namespace MyApp_Services_Orders; // underscores
rules.rationale: Consistent namespace naming enables predictable code organization and discovery.

rules.title: Class and Struct Naming
rules.check: Classes and structs MUST use PascalCase noun phrases describing their responsibility.
rules.bad_example:
public class orderProcessor { } // camelCase
public class ProcessOrders { } // verb phrase
public class OrderHelper { } // vague
rules.rationale: Clear class names communicate purpose at a glance.

rules.title: Interface Naming
rules.check: Interfaces MUST prefix with I and use capability-focused names.
rules.bad_example:
public interface PaymentProcessor { } // Missing I prefix
public interface IStripePaymentImplementation { } // Implementation detail
rules.rationale: I-prefix instantly identifies interfaces. Capability focus enables multiple implementations.

rules.title: Method Naming
rules.check: Methods MUST use PascalCase verb phrases describing the action.
rules.bad_example:
public void orderProcess() { } // camelCase
public void Order() { } // noun only
public void DoIt() { } // vague
rules.rationale: Verb phrases clearly communicate method behavior.

rules.title: Async Method Suffix
rules.check: All async methods MUST end with Async suffix. No exceptions.
rules.bad_example:
public async Task<Order> GetOrder(int id) { } // Missing Async
public async Task ProcessPayment() { } // Missing Async
rules.rationale: Async suffix prevents accidental blocking calls and signals async behavior.

rules.title: Property Naming
rules.check: Properties MUST use PascalCase nouns or adjectives. No Get prefix.
rules.bad_example:
public string firstName { get; set; } // camelCase
public string GetName { get; } // Get prefix
public List<Order> order { get; } // singular for collection
rules.rationale: Property names should read naturally when accessed.

rules.title: Boolean Naming
rules.check: Boolean properties and variables MUST use Is, Has, Can, Should, or Was prefix.
rules.rationale: Prefixes make boolean intent clear and code more readable.

rules.title: Private Field Naming
rules.check: Private fields MUST use _camelCase with underscore prefix.
rules.bad_example:
private readonly ILogger logger; // no prefix
private readonly ILogger _Logger; // PascalCase
private readonly ILogger m_logger; // Hungarian
rules.rationale: Underscore prefix distinguishes fields from parameters and locals.

rules.title: Constant Naming
rules.check: Public constants MUST use PascalCase. Private constants MAY use UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.
rules.bad_example:
public const int max_retries = 3; // snake_case
public const int MAXRETRIES = 3; // no separation
rules.rationale: Public constants follow .NET conventions. Private constants can use traditional constant style.

rules.title: Parameter and Local Variable Naming
rules.check: Parameters and locals MUST use camelCase. No abbreviations except universally known ones.
rules.bad_example:
public void Process(int OrderId, string CustName) { } // PascalCase
public void Process(int oid, string cn) { } // abbreviations
rules.rationale: Descriptive names eliminate guesswork about parameter purpose.

rules.title: Generic Type Parameter Naming
rules.check: Generic type parameters MUST use T prefix with descriptive suffix for complex scenarios.
rules.bad_example:
public class Repository<Entity> { } // no T prefix
public class Cache<K, V> { } // single letters for multiple params
rules.rationale: T-prefix identifies type parameters. Descriptive names clarify purpose.

rules.title: Enum Naming
rules.check: Enums MUST use PascalCase singular names. Values MUST use PascalCase.
rules.bad_example:
public enum OrderStatuses { PENDING, IN_PROGRESS } // plural, UPPER_CASE
public enum orderStatus { pending, inProgress } // camelCase
rules.good_example:
public enum OrderStatus
{
    Pending,
    InProgress,
    Completed,
    Cancelled
}

[Flags]
public enum FilePermissions // Flags are plural
{
    None = 0,
    Read = 1,
    Write = 2,
    Execute = 4
}
rules.rationale: Singular enum names read naturally. Flags use plural to indicate combinability.

rules.title: Event Naming
rules.check: Events MUST use PascalCase past tense for completed actions, present for in-progress.
rules.bad_example:
public event EventHandler OrderCreate; // present tense for completed
public event EventHandler OnOrderCreated; // On prefix (old style)
rules.rationale: Tense indicates whether event fires before or after action.

rules.title: Extension Method Class Naming
rules.check: Extension method classes MUST use {Type}Extensions naming pattern.
rules.bad_example:
public static class Helpers { } // vague
public static class StringUtils { } // Utils suffix
rules.rationale: Consistent naming makes extension methods discoverable.

rules.title: Test Method Naming
rules.check: Test methods MUST follow Method_Scenario_ExpectedResult pattern.
rules.rationale: Descriptive test names serve as documentation and failure context.

rules.title: Record Naming
rules.check: Records MUST use PascalCase with appropriate suffixes for purpose.
rules.bad_example:
public record orderDto(string Name); // camelCase
public record OrderData(string Name); // vague suffix
rules.rationale: Suffixes clarify record purpose (DTO, Request, Response, Event, Summary).

rules.title: No Hungarian notation (strName, intCount)
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No Hungarian notation (strName, intCount)

rules.title: No single-letter names except loop counters and lambdas
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No single-letter names except loop counters and lambdas

rules.title: No abbreviations unless universally known (Id, Url, Http, Xml, Json)
rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No abbreviations unless universally known (Id, Url, Http, Xml, Json)

rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No `Get` prefix on properties

rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No underscores in public identifiers

rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No inconsistent casing within project

rules.check: FORBIDDEN: No bool properties without Is/Has/Can/Should prefix
